newsitem.title: USA: McCurry lobbies for seat on Princeton board.
newsitem.headline: McCurry lobbies for seat on Princeton board.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry jokingly lobbied to join Princeton University's board of trustees Wednesday as a reward for persuading President Bill Clinton to speak at its 250th anniversary last year.

A member of Princeton's class of 1976, McCurry was drawn into a discussion of the university when asked if he knew where Chelsea Clinton planned to attend college and whether he had lobbied on behalf of his alma mater.

"I won't deny that I have discussed the subject with young Ms. Clinton, but I would heavily deny that I lobbied on behalf of any particular institution," McCurry told reporters, adding that he did not know whether she had yet made a choice.
He was then asked jokingly what Princeton did for alumni who delivered major guests for university functions, prompting McCurry's tongue-in-cheek reply: "They reward them heartily.

"For example, when one delivers the president of the United States for the 250th commencement anniversary ... one would hope that eventually it would lead to a position on the board of trustees or something," he said. "I ain't there yet."
